body: I see the same behaviour in Chrome 44 and Chrome Canary (V8 4.6). @lazutkin Do you want to open a V8 issue here: https://code.google.com/p/v8/issues/list
Closing, nothing io.js itself can do. :)
We're going in to LTS with this version of V8, I hope this isn't going to bite us in a similar way to `Array.values()` in 0.12, perhaps this should be part of our "Known issues"?
Yeah perhaps we should document it. It's not a thing that perviously existed though (afaik) so I think we're good there.

This seems worrying, especially that it's available by default, not behind a flag. Comments in [the V8 issue](https://code.google.com/p/v8/issues/detail?id=4387) suggest the fix for that will be a one-liner. I somehow missed that Node 4.0.0 will use v8 4.4, not 4.5 (i.e. the same as io.js 3) but since v8 4.4 will soon lose upstream support perhaps patching this on the Node.js side wouldn't introduce big issues?

I'd not be opposed to floating a patch on v8 for this when they drop support for 4.4 upstream because we're going to have to be supporting this version for some time and will be adding our own patches to it anyway. I don't see this as being a huge problem, at least initially, but perhaps as folks start using computed properties for newer versions of node and v4 LTS starts to get a bit old we could end up in hot water.
I'm fine with just leaving a note about it I think.
Going to reopen this to catch issues that will inevitably be files about this.

body: It seems V8 might get the patch backported [even to v4.5](https://code.google.com/p/v8/issues/detail?id=4387#c18) even though Chrome 45 should be coming within the next 2 weeks; this indicates that the V8 team either treats this problem as serious or the patch as very safe. Most likely the only reason it's not getting backported to 4.4 upstream is that it will be EOL'd on the V8 side soon.

The V8 team would like to 'bake' this change a bit in canary before it gets back-ported to stable. It is likely that V8 4.4 will be EOL'd by that time, but it should be easy to float this fix on Node v4.

> but it should be easy to float this fix on Node v4

:+1:

The fix has been backported to v8 4.6. Chrome 45 is out with buggy computed props but it's still planned to backport the patch to v8 4.5 if it proves to be fine on 4.6.

This is most likely the day v8 4.4 is EOL'd upstream.

@Fishrock123 handed this one over in the interests of expediting it since it's been blocked and waiting for >4 days now. So this is taking over from #2607 with a proposed CHANGELOG.md.

Testing now, will move forward to release as soon as I've done basic smoke tests.
## 2015-09-02, Version 3.3.0, @rvagg
### Notable changes
- **build**: Add a `--link-module` option to `configure` that can be used to bundle additional JavaScript modules into a built binary (Bradley Meck) [#2497](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/2497)
- **docs**: Merge outstanding doc updates from joyent/node (James M Snell) [#2378](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/2378)
- **http_parser**: Significant performance improvement by having `http.Server` consume all initial data from its `net.Socket` and parsing directly without having to enter JavaScript. Any `'data'` listeners on the `net.Socket` will result in the data being "unconsumed" into JavaScript, thereby undoing any performance gains. (Fedor Indutny) [#2355](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/2355)
- **V8**: Upgrade to 4.4.63.30 (from 4.4.63.26) (Michaël Zasso) [#2482](https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/2482)
### Known issues

See https://github.com/nodejs/io.js/labels/confirmed-bug for complete and current list of known issues.
- Some uses of computed object shorthand properties are not handled correctly by the current version of V8. e.g. `[{ [prop]: val }]` evaluates to `[{}]`. [#2507](https://github.com/nodejs/node/issues/2507)
- Some problems with unreferenced timers running during `beforeExit` are still to be resolved. See [#1264](https://github.com/nodejs/io.js/issues/1264).
- Surrogate pair in REPL can freeze terminal. [#690](https://github.com/nodejs/io.js/issues/690)
- `process.send()` is not synchronous as the docs suggest, a regression introduced in 1.0.2, see [#760](https://github.com/nodejs/io.js/issues/760).
- Calling `dns.setServers()` while a DNS query is in progress can cause the process to crash on a failed assertion. [#894](https://github.com/nodejs/io.js/issues/894)
- `url.resolve` may transfer the auth portion of the url when resolving between two full hosts, see [#1435](https://github.com/nodejs/io.js/issues/1435).
